speaker: Unknown
en: Good afternoon, everybody.
zh: 大家下午好。

speaker: Unknown
en: My name is Garrett.
zh: 我叫 Garrett。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am on the product team at WorkOS.
zh: 我在 WorkOS 的产品团队工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you may see that the title of this talk has slightly changed.
zh: 你们可能注意到这场演讲的标题有了一点变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the bad news.
zh: 这是个坏消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: The good news is that the talk is better for it because the original idea I had for this talk two months ago is already sort of out of date with how quickly things move.
zh: 好消息是，演讲因此变得更好了，因为我两个月前为这场演讲想出的原始构想，以事物发展的速度来看，已经有点过时了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So today we're going to talk about how do we enable anyone at your company to ship.
zh: 所以今天我们要谈的是，如何让你公司的任何人都能把东西交付出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are lots of people at your company that have great ideas of things that will solve problems inside your company.
zh: 你公司里有很多人，他们有很多好点子，能解决公司内部的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even with AI, the technology still holds them back.
zh: 但即便有了 AI，技术仍然在拖他们的后腿。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to tell you the story of how we dealt with this problem, what we did about it, and give you some advice if you're going to do it yourself or talk about what we're going to offer to help folks with this problem.
zh: 所以我想给你们讲讲我们如何处理这个问题的故事，我们为此做了什么，并且如果你们想自己做的话给一些建议，或者谈谈我们打算提供什么来帮助大家解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this was about six, eight months ago.
zh: 这大概是六到八个月之前的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of our account executives, Perona, she was about to go on maternity leave.
zh: 我们的一位客户经理 Perona，她当时即将休产假。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's an incredible AE, and she wanted to build something to help the rest of the sales team while she was on leave.
zh: 她是一位非常出色的 AE，她想构建一些东西来帮助她在休假期间的销售团队其他人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So she went and built something called Perona GPT.
zh: 于是她去构建了一个叫 Perona GPT 的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's basically a chatbot trained on her sales calls and all the stuff she knew about the product to help other people while she was out.
zh: 它基本上是一个聊天机器人，用她的销售电话以及她对产品的所有了解进行训练，在她不在的时候帮助其他人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So she went, she built this at the time.
zh: 于是她就去做了，她在当时构建了这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: She used Lovable, all this stuff.
zh: 她用的是 Lovable，诸如此类的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: She got it working.
zh: 她把它做能用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: She shared it and said, hey, I have this tool that you can use while I'm out.
zh: 她把它分享出去说，嘿，我有一个工具，你们在我休假期间可以用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope it's helpful.
zh: 希望它有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: First thing, our CEO, Michael, tries to use the tool, and he gets this, you don't have access, he doesn't have a lovable account, because he's not used lovable, and so he can't use it.
zh: 第一件事，我们的 CEO Michael 试着去用这个工具，他遇到了这个——你没有访问权限，他没有 Lovable 账号，因为他没用过 Lovable，所以他没法用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he's like, hey, what can we do here?
zh: 于是他就说，嘿，我们这里能做点什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we make sure everyone can use it?
zh: 我们怎么确保所有人都能用它？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the solution was,
zh: 于是解决方案是，

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, two engineers on our Applied AI team, can you go convert this into an app that we can deploy and that we can give everyone access to?
zh: 嘿，我们 Applied AI 团队的两位工程师，你们能不能去把这个转换成一个我们可以部署的应用，并且能给所有人访问权限？

speaker: Unknown
en: So now we have an account exec who comes up with a great idea.
zh: 所以现在我们有一位客户经理，她想到了一个很棒的点子。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in order to make that idea actually useful, we have to go get engineers to spend a bunch of time, recode it, move it from lovable, deploy it, manage it, all this kind of stuff.
zh: 但为了让这个点子真正有用，我们得去找工程师花一大堆时间，重新写代码，把它从 Lovable 上迁移下来，部署它，管理它，所有这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is really painful, because what should happen is she creates the app, deploys it, shares it, everyone gets access, and now people are using it.
zh: 这真的很痛苦，因为本应发生的是她创建应用，部署它，分享它，所有人都获得访问权限，然后大家就开始用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so building things got cheap.
zh: 所以构建东西变得便宜了。

speaker: Unknown
en: She was using Lovable.
zh: 她当时在用 Lovable。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was right around when Opus 4.8 was coming out.
zh: 那差不多就是 Opus 4.8 发布的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now people are using Claude Code, Codex, and stuff in many cases.
zh: 现在很多情况下大家在用 Claude Code、Codex 之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's not hard to build a thing, something that you can npm run dev.
zh: 所以构建一个东西并不难，一个你能 npm run dev 的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's pretty easy now.
zh: 这现在已经很容易了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But shipping it, making it available, even internally to your company, hasn't really gotten that much easier, right?
zh: 但把它交付出去，让它可用，哪怕只是在公司内部可用，并没有变得那么容易，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do you deploy this?
zh: 你要把它部署到哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where are you going to run this app?
zh: 你要到哪里去运行这个应用？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you ensure it's secure, right?
zh: 你如何确保它是安全的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: How are people going to, you want to all have your internal employees authenticate to it, but you don't want it to be publicly available.
zh: 人们要怎么……你希望所有内部员工都对它进行身份验证，但你不希望它公开可访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, for a less technical person, for a non-engineer, they're going to struggle with, you know, do I put it on Vercel?
zh: 所以，你知道，对于一个技术能力较弱的人，对于非工程师来说，他们会纠结于，你知道，我是不是该把它放到 Vercel 上？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I don't have access to a Vercel account or a Cloudflare account because I'm not an engineer.
zh: 可我没有 Vercel 账号或 Cloudflare 账号的访问权限，因为我不是工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: They might not know the details of how to do that.
zh: 他们可能不知道怎么做的细节。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even for engineers who know how these tools work, they don't really want to have to go through this and do it from scratch every single time.
zh: 即便是懂这些工具如何工作的工程师，他们也不真的想每次都从头经历一遍这些流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if you're deploying these things internally, you want them to have auth and security baked in.
zh: 而且如果你在内部部署这些东西，你会希望它们内置了身份验证和安全性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't want people just shipping API keys to stuff that might get checked into code bases or stuff like that.
zh: 你不希望人们随便把 API 密钥发布出去，可能会被提交进代码库或者类似的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what do you do?
zh: 那么你该怎么办？

speaker: Unknown
en: You end up burning a bunch of engineering time to say, hey, this is important.
zh: 你最终会烧掉一大堆工程时间来说，嘿，这个很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to go convert this to be some proper app deployment.
zh: 我们需要把它转换成一个正式的应用部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the thing we needed at WorkOS was kind of two things.
zh: 所以我们在 WorkOS 需要的东西大概有两样。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, the capability for everyone at the company to build and ship an application.
zh: 第一，让公司里的每个人都能构建并发布一个应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: They shouldn't need to go ask infra for provisioning.
zh: 他们不应该需要去找 infra 申请资源开通。

speaker: Unknown
en: They shouldn't need to get security approval for standard apps.
zh: 对于标准应用，他们不应该需要获得安全审批。

speaker: Unknown
en: They should just be able to build the thing and make it available.
zh: 他们应该直接就能把东西构建出来并让它可用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And two, we want a distribution.
zh: 第二，我们想要分发能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: As soon as they ship it, they can link someone else to it.
zh: 他们一发布，就能把链接发给其他人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That person can click the link in Slack, open it up, and access the application without any red flags or any kind of red tape.
zh: 那个人可以在 Slack 里点击链接，打开它，直接访问这个应用，不需要任何危险信号或任何形式的繁文缛节。

speaker: Unknown
en: We wanted to move fast.
zh: 我们想快速行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: We wanted to build quickly.
zh: 我们想快速构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have this applied AI team at WorkOS whose their singular job is, how do we make AI more and more useful across the company?
zh: 我们在 WorkOS 有一个应用 AI 团队，他们的唯一工作就是：我们如何让 AI 在整个公司范围内越来越有用？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not just how do we move the software development process along, make engineers useful with AI, but how do we make everyone useful with AI?
zh: 不仅仅是推动软件开发流程、让工程师用 AI 更高效，而是如何让每个人都用 AI 更高效？

speaker: Unknown
en: Building is cheap, right?
zh: 构建很便宜，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We could build a thing, no problem, but how do we know it works?
zh: 我们可以构建一个东西，没问题，但我们怎么知道它有效？

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to get the feedback around it.
zh: 我们需要获得围绕它的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turns out we basically had sort of a forcing function to gather feedback, which is we started doing these company-wide Claude days.
zh: 结果发现，我们基本上有一种收集反馈的强制机制，那就是我们开始举办全公司的 Claude 日。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, it's a single-day hackathon where everyone pairs up into teams and builds an app.
zh: 基本上，这是一个为期一天的黑客马拉松，大家两人一组组成团队，构建一个应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And typically, when we do this, we actually pair non-engineers with engineers.
zh: 而且通常，当我们做这件事时，我们实际上是让非工程师和工程师配对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we actually have the non-engineers do the building.
zh: 而且我们实际上是让非工程师来做构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're the ones that have our hands on keyboard.
zh: 他们才是真正动手操作键盘的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're the ones building the application, while the engineer that's paired with them is there to consult, help them, unblock them with any issues they find so they don't get stuck, kind of be a sounding board for how they can approach this.
zh: 他们是构建应用的人，而与他们配对的工程师在那里提供咨询、帮助他们、解决他们遇到的任何问题以免他们卡住，有点像是他们如何着手这件事的参谋。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we have a ton of our marketing folks and sales folks that have all these really great ideas of apps that they've maybe struggled to bring to life.
zh: 我们有大量的市场同事和销售同事，他们有很多非常好的应用创意，但可能一直难以把它们变为现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we built two things.
zh: 所以我们构建了两样东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first thing is we built a CLI.
zh: 第一件事是我们构建了一个 CLI。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call it WOW.
zh: 我们叫它 WOW。

speaker: Unknown
en: WOW is the thing that helps you build and generate an app without needing to know any of the underlying details.
zh: WOW 是帮你构建和生成一个应用的东西，不需要了解任何底层细节。

speaker: Unknown
en: It basically is a toolkit that helps you set up Git, set up a repo, clone in an example application that you can use to start with for Claude Code or Codex to build the app you want to build.
zh: 它基本上是一个工具包，帮你设置 Git、设置仓库、克隆一个示例应用，你可以用它作为起点，让 Claude Code 或 Codex 来构建你想构建的应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we distribute it to every single employee at the company through our MDM.
zh: 我们通过我们的 MDM 把它分发给公司的每一位员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just push it on your machine so every employee, day one, has access to this tool.
zh: 我们直接把它推送到你的机器上，所以每位员工从第一天起就能使用这个工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: The WoW CLI lets you run things like WoW App Create.
zh: WoW CLI 让你可以运行诸如 WoW App Create 之类的命令。

speaker: Unknown
en: What it does is that you name the app, it scans your machine and says, okay, do you have Git installed?
zh: 它的作用是：你给应用起个名字，它会扫描你的机器并检查，好的，你装了 Git 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you logged into GitHub?
zh: 你登录 GitHub 了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have Doppler, which is where you do secrets management?
zh: 你有 Doppler 吗，就是那个做密钥管理的工具？

speaker: Unknown
en: It kind of does all this pre-configuration of your developer machine, whether you're an engineer or not, so that everything is kind of ready to go and you're not going to hit any snags along the way.
zh: 它会对你的开发机做所有这些预配置，不管你是不是工程师，这样一切都准备就绪，你在过程中不会遇到任何阻碍。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also built a shared skills repository.
zh: 我们还构建了一个共享技能仓库。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anyone at the company can, if they've built a skill that's useful, they can push that skill up, and it's shared to everyone, and then it's easy to fetch those skills, see what's available, and pull skills down to help you build things or do certain workflows.
zh: 所以公司里任何人，如果他们构建了一个有用的技能，就可以把这个技能推上去，它会被分享给所有人，然后很容易获取这些技能、查看有哪些可用的，并把技能拉下来帮助你构建东西或完成某些工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm going to do a quick demo to kind of show you a little bit of what this looks like.
zh: 所以我要做一个快速演示，给你们稍微展示一下这是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So here I'm in this folder, and I want to create an app.
zh: 这里我在这个文件夹里，我想创建一个应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's do AIE demo.
zh: 就做 AIE demo 吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it basically runs through this whole flow.
zh: 然后它基本上会跑完整个流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've already obviously configured my machine.
zh: 显然我已经配置好我的机器了。 [[这不是我第一次做这件事。]]

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not the first time I'm doing this.
zh: 这不是我第一次做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it checks.
zh: 所以它会检查。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have Git.
zh: 我有 Git。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have Node, GitHub, Doppler.
zh: 我有 Node、GitHub、Doppler。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm signed in, everything.
zh: 我已登录，一切就绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what it does is actually creates a repo in our enterprise GitHub account.
zh: 而它实际做的是在我们的企业 GitHub 账户里创建一个仓库。

speaker: Unknown
en: It uses a kind of template that we already have defined.
zh: 它使用一个我们已经定义好的模板。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it starts out with basically a kind of blank Node.js app.
zh: 所以它一开始基本上是一个空白 Node.js 应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it does that, pushes everything, runs it, and then now we get something that I can run internally or locally.
zh: 它完成这些，推送所有内容，运行它，然后现在我们就得到一个我可以在内部或本地运行的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does a little deploy step, and then we get something available at localhost that I can pull up here.
zh: 它会做一个小小的部署步骤，然后我们就有了一个可以在 localhost 上访问的东西，我可以在这里把它打开。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have this internal app example.
zh: 我们有这个内部应用示例。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's not obvious, we're running this on Cloudflare because it makes it really easy to quickly deploy a Node app.
zh: 如果不明显的话,我们是把它跑在 Cloudflare 上的,因为它让快速部署一个 Node 应用变得非常简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is great.
zh: 所以这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Single command.
zh: 一条命令。

speaker: Unknown
en: I now have this app running.
zh: 我现在就有这个应用在运行了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then from that point on, I can just pop into Claude and say, hey, I'm doing a demo for AIE.
zh: 然后从那时起,我可以直接打开 Claude 说,嘿,我要给 AIE 做个演示。

speaker: Unknown
en: What can we put in this app that would be cool?
zh: 我们能在这个应用里放点什么酷的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm going to let this go off.
zh: 所以我就让它跑起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to see what it does.
zh: 我们等着看它会做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is sort of just Claude being Claude.
zh: 这有点像是 Claude 做它自己会做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I want to walk through a few parts of what we've built and some examples of the things we've built.
zh: 但我想讲一讲我们构建的一些部分,以及我们构建的一些东西的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have this internal registry.
zh: 我们有这个内部 registry。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anytime you push an app with WoW, we actually log into this internal registry.
zh: 每当你用 WoW 推送一个应用,我们实际上会记录到这个内部 registry 里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can see we have 278 apps that have been pushed, 21 that had a deployment done today.
zh: 你们可以看到,我们已经推送了 278 个应用,今天有 21 个完成了部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: Over the last week, we've had 3.3 million requests go through these applications.
zh: 在过去一周里,有 330 万个请求通过了这些应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these aren't just little dashboard tools.
zh: 所以这些不只是小小的仪表盘工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're also APIs, Slack bots, and things that we've created and use internally ourselves.
zh: 它们还包括 API、Slack 机器人,以及我们自己创建并在内部使用的各种东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then 60 of these are on sort of custom domains, so they have their own branded domain name.
zh: 而其中 60 个跑在某种自定义域名上,所以它们有自己的品牌域名。

speaker: Unknown
en: A couple examples of things we've built is Connor on our product marketing team.
zh: 我们构建的东西的几个例子:我们产品营销团队的 Connor。

speaker: Unknown
en: We send these monthly newsletters that are like, hey, what's the latest in Work OS?
zh: 我们每月会发这些新闻通讯,比如「嘿,Work OS 最近有什么新动态?」

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of a pain.
zh: 这挺麻烦的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to take updates that we have, put them into a format, and then we need to format them to send in both Slack and over email, which is pretty annoying.
zh: 我们得把已有的更新放成一种格式,然后再把它们排版成既能在 Slack 又能通过邮件发送的形式,这相当烦人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we built this, I think my auth.
zh: 所以我们构建了这个,我想先弄下我的 auth。

speaker: Unknown
en: So here's how these apps are protected, right?
zh: 这些应用是这样被保护的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to log in with my Okta account in order to access them.
zh: 我必须用我的 Okta 账号登录才能访问它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you go to any of these URLs you'll see, you won't be able to get to them.
zh: 所以如果你访问这些 URL 中的任何一个,你会发现你进不去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So here, it basically pulls in all of our changelogs.
zh: 这里,它基本上会把我们所有的 changelog 拉进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can curate that.
zh: 你可以对其进行筛选。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can design what the Slack message is going to look like.
zh: 你可以设计 Slack 消息将会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's a kind of singular place to design this experience.
zh: 所以它是一个用来设计这整套体验的单一场所。

speaker: Unknown
en: A thing that I built is we have a changelog, changelog, workOS.com slash changelogs where we post all our updates.
zh: 我构建的一个东西是,我们有一个 changelog,changelog.workOS.com/changelogs,我们在上面发布所有更新。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we do this through Webflow, which is like a CMS platform.
zh: 我们通过 Webflow 来做这件事,它像一个 CMS 平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's pretty painful to actually
zh: 实际操作起来挺痛苦的——

speaker: Unknown
en: Go in, design the changelog post, and do all of this stuff.
zh: 进去、设计 changelog 帖子、做完所有这些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I built a tool that basically allows anyone at our company to draft these changelogs, and so someone can come in.
zh: 所以我构建了一个工具,基本上让我们公司的任何人都能起草这些 changelog,这样某人就可以进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ooh.
zh: 哦。

speaker: Unknown
en: I gotta refresh my auth.
zh: 我得刷新一下我的 auth。

speaker: Unknown
en: There we go.
zh: 好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyone can come in, kind of draft these changelogs, and then it posts into Slack so I can know, hey, there's a new changelog, someone's drafted up, I can review it, and then when it's ready, I can post it, and it posts it live.
zh: 任何人都可以进来,起草这些 changelog,然后它会发到 Slack,这样我就能知道,嘿,有个新的 changelog,有人起草好了,我可以审阅它,等它就绪后,我可以发布它,然后它就会正式上线。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is the kind of tools that we're able to build.
zh: 所以这就是我们能够构建的这类工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, anyone at our company can now spin up Claude Code, build out that they want, and deploy it live, make it available to the entire company.
zh: 基本上,我们公司的任何人现在都可以启动 Claude Code,构建他们想要的东西,然后实时部署,让它对全公司可用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to let that just sit in the background.
zh: 我就让它继续在后台跑着。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't need to see what that does.
zh: 我们不需要看它做了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah.
zh: 不过是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the kind of idea.
zh: 大概就是这个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we have tons of people at the company building these tools.
zh: 现在我们公司有很多人在构建这类工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing gets in the way.
zh: 没有任何东西挡路。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't have to ask for, hey, can someone deploy this?
zh: 他们不需要去问,嘿,有人能部署这个吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, can someone provision some account for me?
zh: 嘿,有人能帮我开通一个账号吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone by default in the company can use this tool.
zh: 公司里每个人默认都可以使用这个工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to talk a little bit about Atlas, which is the actual platform underneath this that empowers this tool.
zh: 所以我想稍微谈一下 Atlas,它是在这个工具之下赋能这个工具的实际平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: WoW is just sort of the CLI that people use to interface with it, but Atlas is actually the underlying infrastructure.
zh: WoW 只是人们用来与它交互的 CLI,但 Atlas 实际上是底层基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, Atlas allows you to create, build, deploy, and share these applications.
zh: 基本上，Atlas 让你能够创建、构建、部署和分享这些应用程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: The sort of three principles when we were building Atlas that we wanted to maintain and ensure that provided a great experience.
zh: 这就是我们在构建 Atlas 时想要保持并确保提供良好体验的三条原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: One was we wanted the infrared to be invisible.
zh: 第一是我们希望基础设施是不可见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one should need to know where the deployment target is.
zh: 任何人都不需要知道部署目标在哪里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It happens to be that we're running on Cloudflare workers.
zh: 碰巧我们运行在 Cloudflare workers 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: If at some point we want to change that to Vercel or AWS, it shouldn't matter.
zh: 如果在某个时候我们想把它换成 Vercel 或 AWS,那也不应该有影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: It should be transparent to anyone trying to build and deploy these applications.
zh: 对任何试图构建和部署这些应用程序的人来说，这都应该是透明的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to be secured by default.
zh: 我们希望默认是安全的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't want to risk those.
zh: 我们不想冒那些风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't show you all of the apps that we built.
zh: 我没法给你们展示我们构建的所有应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them have a lot of PII.
zh: 其中一些包含大量 PII。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're customer tools, sales tools that we use.
zh: 它们是客户工具、我们使用的销售工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we don't want anyone to just be able to access these tools outside the company because they're very sensitive.
zh: 所以我们不希望公司以外的任何人都能访问这些工具，因为它们非常敏感。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then last is the discoverability.
zh: 然后最后是可发现性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone shares a link in Slack.
zh: 有人在 Slack 里分享一个链接。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyone should be able to click that and be able to view that tool.
zh: 任何人都应该能够点开它并查看那个工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: So today Atlas runs on Cloudflare's developer platform.
zh: 所以今天 Atlas 运行在 Cloudflare 的开发者平台上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every app, when you run that wow create step, provides compute, storage with D1 databases, KV values, all the bits and pieces you need.
zh: 每个应用，当你运行那个 wow create 步骤时，都会提供计算、带 D1 数据库的存储、KV 值，以及你需要的所有零碎组件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you don't have to ask, like, oh, well, if I need to store persistent data, am I going to be able to do that?
zh: 所以你不用去问，比如，哦，如果我需要存储持久化数据，我能做到吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's already part of the package.
zh: 它已经是这个包的一部分了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we automatically host all of these tools when you push them under workos.tools.
zh: 而且当你推送这些工具时，我们会自动把它们托管在 workos.tools 之下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have this shared domain that whatever your app is called, you get that host name underneath workos.tools.
zh: 所以我们有一个共享域名，无论你的应用叫什么名字，你都会得到 workos.tools 之下的那个主机名。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you don't have to worry about where is the app going to be available, how does it get, you know, do people get access.
zh: 所以你不用担心应用会在哪里可用、它是怎么被获取的、你知道的，人们是否能够获得访问权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: Secure by default.
zh: 默认安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: So all of these apps are automatically protected by our Okta SSO account.
zh: 所以所有这些应用都自动受到我们 Okta SSO 账户的保护。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can't log in if you don't have access to our Okta account.
zh: 所以如果你没有我们 Okta 账户的访问权限，你就无法登录。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've actually built for APIs and Slackbots.
zh: 对于 API 和 Slackbot,我们实际上做了构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've built a way to actually plug holes for a token-based authentication.
zh: 我们构建了一种方式，可以实际为基于令牌的身份验证开洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if that's something you need, you can build out.
zh: 所以如果这是你需要的，你可以构建出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can kind of enable that and then get API access for some of these tools that we're using.
zh: 你可以启用它，然后为我们正在使用的一些工具获得 API 访问权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the requests are logged and auditable.
zh: 所有请求都会被记录并且可审计。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have logs of all the traffic that's happening.
zh: 所以我们有所有流量的日志。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we think there was some sort of leak or security issue, we can go and detect what happened.
zh: 所以如果我们认为发生了某种泄露或安全问题，我们可以去查明发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then all the secrets.
zh: 然后还有所有的密钥。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you need API access to any of our tools, internal tools or third-party tools, that's all stored securely.
zh: 所以如果你需要对我们的任何工具、内部工具或第三方工具进行 API 访问，这些都被安全地存储。

speaker: Unknown
en: We use Doppler in this case.
zh: 在这种情况下我们使用 Doppler。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you don't really have to do secrets management.
zh: 所以你基本上不需要做密钥管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to worry about, did I push a secret into the Git repo?
zh: 你不必担心，我是不是把一个密钥推送到了 Git 仓库里？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's now a problem.
zh: 那现在不是问题了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's all done securely.
zh: 一切都安全地完成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then last, we have the catalog for discovery.
zh: 然后最后，我们有用于发现的目录。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every app's discoverable.
zh: 每个应用都是可发现的。

speaker: Unknown
en: No need to share.
zh: 不需要分享。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't need to have sharing support because you by default have access.
zh: 我们不需要支持分享功能，因为你默认就有访问权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think so far I showed you that catalog page which had a few hundred apps.
zh: 所以我想到目前为止我给你看了那个有几百个应用的目录页面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously not every single app is super important and sees the light of day.
zh: 显然不是每一个应用都超级重要、都能见到天日。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we have about 60 apps that are been deployed, maintained, or getting used on a regular basis.
zh: 但我们大约有 60 个应用被部署、维护，或者正在被定期使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this isn't just like two tools people built that are useful.
zh: 所以这不像只是人们构建的两个有用的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually becoming a way in which things are being maintained.
zh: 它实际上正在成为事物被维护的一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually had someone build a tool where
zh: 我们实际上有一个人构建了一个工具，

speaker: Unknown
en: You take any arbitrary HTML, upload it, and it gives you a shared link.
zh: 你拿任意 HTML，上传上去，它就会给你一个共享链接。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's basically like a mini-hoster of like mocks or diagrams or things that you can easily share.
zh: 所以它基本上就像一个 mini-hoster，可以托管 mock、图表或那些你能轻松分享的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're seeing over 3 million requests a week run through all of these apps.
zh: 我们看到每周有超过 300 万个请求通过所有这些应用运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is partially users using traffic, but it's also one of our tools, Wallaby, is like a sales tool.
zh: 这部分是用户在使用流量，但它也是我们的一个工具 Wallaby，是一个销售工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we actually built APIs for that that allows us to access that data in other systems, in Slack.
zh: 而且我们实际上为它构建了 API，让我们可以在其他系统中、在 Slack 中访问那些数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's not just humans accessing this data, it's machines and agents as well.
zh: 所以不仅仅是人类在访问这些数据，机器和智能体也在访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've completely eliminated the need for asking for help in deploying applications because nothing stops anyone anymore.
zh: 我们已经完全消除了在部署应用时寻求帮助的需求，因为再也没有什么能阻挡任何人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the most important metric is our goal was enable non-engineers to build and deploy apps.
zh: 而且我认为最重要的指标是，我们的目标是让非工程师能够构建和部署应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And out of our apps, out of these 60 apps, 37% of them have been built without any engineers in any of the commits.
zh: 在我们的应用中，在这 60 个应用中，37% 的应用在所有 commit 中都没有任何工程师参与构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they're totally built between that person and Claude without engineering involvement.
zh: 所以它们完全是由那个人和 Claude 构建的，没有任何工程参与。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's sort of the marker of a true success here that we've actually eliminated the need for, hey, some engineer, can you migrate this tool?
zh: 而这差不多就是真正成功的标志——我们确实消除了「嘿，哪位工程师，你能帮我迁移这个工具吗？」的需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you manage this tool on behalf of marketing or sales?
zh: 「你能替市场部或销售部管理这个工具吗？」

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's more that we want to do here.
zh: 所以我们在这里还想做更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is sort of an initial version.
zh: 这差不多是一个初始版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to add granular auth.
zh: 我们想添加细粒度的鉴权。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not every app should necessarily be open by default to everyone in the company, obviously.
zh: 显然，不是每个应用都应该默认对公司的所有人开放。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some sensitive data in some cases.
zh: 有些情况下存在一些敏感数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we want to add, we already know who the user is when they're logging to the app.
zh: 所以我们想添加——当用户登录应用时，我们已经知道他们是谁了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we want to support doing kind of like group-based, role-based permissions for these apps easily.
zh: 所以我们想支持轻松地为这些应用做基于组、基于角色的权限控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: We wanted more data integration.
zh: 我们想要更多的数据集成。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we kind of already have this capability aspect to WoW and to Atlas where if I need access to our Snowflake data, for example, I don't need to go kind of think about API keys.
zh: 所以我们已经让 WoW 和 Atlas 具备了某种能力层面的东西，比如如果需要访问我们的 Snowflake 数据，我不需要去琢磨 API 密钥。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can just say I want to add Snowflake.
zh: 我可以直接说我想添加 Snowflake。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now the app has correctly maintained Snowflake access.
zh: 然后这个应用就正确地获得了维护好的 Snowflake 访问权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the other thing that we're building out is Slack integration.
zh: 然后我们正在构建的另一件事是 Slack 集成。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of these tools are great, but you really want them to be available inside Slack so that someone can just app the tool and answer a question, get use out of it, or actually drive a workflow.
zh: 这些工具中很多都很棒，但你真的希望它们能在 Slack 内可用，这样有人就可以直接调用这个工具、回答一个问题、从中获得价值，或者真正驱动一个工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're building included Slack integration.
zh: 所以我们正在构建内置的 Slack 集成。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if someone deploys an app, they can also get the Slack app automatically installed.
zh: 这样如果有人部署了一个应用，他们也可以自动安装 Slack 应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, we're kind of experiencing ourselves a revolution in internal app development.
zh: 对我们来说，我们正在亲身经历一场内部应用开发的革命。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've used other platforms to build certain tools.
zh: 我们用过其他平台来构建某些工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've always found them very cumbersome.
zh: 我们一直觉得它们非常笨重。

speaker: Unknown
en: They basically still took engineers to build and maintain, and it sort of limited the tools that we could build.
zh: 它们基本上仍然需要工程师来构建和维护，这在某种程度上限制了我们可以构建的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, AI solved the build problem, but we needed more in order to make this a ubiquitous platform for our team.
zh: 对我们来说，AI 解决了构建问题，但要让这成为我们团队的一个无处不在的平台，我们还需要更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Atlas provides its capabilities to enable anyone at our company to ship internal apps.
zh: Atlas 提供其能力，让我们公司的任何人都能发布内部应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're interested in having this kind of capability at your company, I'd love to talk to you about it.
zh: 如果你有兴趣在你的公司拥有这种能力，我很乐意和你聊聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。
